An appropriate successor to The Static Speaks My Name. Bucket Detective is bizarre and macabre, and while it's a bit longer than Barksdale's first game, it doesn't overstay its welcome. As with Static, this game is mostly a walking simulator - a few light puzzles, "bring Key A to Lock B," etc - but unlike its predecessor, Bucket Detective takes you through a coherent plot, rather than leaving you to piece together vague context clues. I think both approaches work, and didn't find myself favoring one game over the other

Bucket Detective also has a bit more humor in it, and as with all humor (especially "dark" humor) your mileage may vary. I found some of the tongue-in-cheek gags a bit self-congratulatory, while other more understated or deadpan moments were genuinely funny

It's clear from this game that Barksdale has a lot of interesting ideas about both narrative and game design - as with Static, I really recommend listening to his developer commentary. It's got some really surprising insights into the process of making a game, even a relatively simple one. Not sure if he's planning on making anything else in the future, but I'd be very interested to see it

[h1]What the Buck-et Detective?[/h1]

[b]Bucket Detective[/b] is a short yet disturbing horror game by Jesse Barksdale, creator of The Static Speaks My Name. It is an unsettling narrative experience with a variety of moral dilemmas for the player to face, the combinations of which produce multiple endings. The game can be completed in its entirety in a little over an hour but still manages to pack a punch and has the ability to leave players feeling anything from confused and amused to downright offended.

This game is certainly a unique experience but it is also not for everyone. The artwork is inappropriately cute and the narrative is thought-provoking but the combination of elements make the complete experience really quite sinister. Overall, it is an enjoyable but troubling and confusing experience that requires minimal investment in terms of either time or money that I’d very cautiously recommend it to anyone not of an overly sensitive disposition.

Bucket Detective is a bizarre game made by the same guy that created The static speaks my name, so you know that you're in for a weird game.

Story:

You play as David Davids. David is a perverted old man whose only goal in life is to finish his novel called Bucket Detective, so he can get girls to have sex with him, but sadly he doesn't have any good ideas and he finds that writing the book is difficult, but a friend of his directs him towards an old building where he has to complete a few goals and after completing them he will get his wish.

Bucket Detective is a weird game and the keyword is weird. If you played The static speaks my name, you know what to expect. Bucket Detective is just as weird and just as disturbing (maybe even more so,I won't spoil, but trust me some of the things you find out are really disturbing). The story is weird and a bit offensive, but it's intriguing to say the least. 

Graphics: 

The graphics in Bucket Detective are really simplistic as all you do is explore a building and walk around rooms that give off the feel like the building was abandoned. Even though I feel like the graphics are simplistic there's sort of a charm about it that I really like. I also love the art style in the intro and ending cutscenes that give me vibes of an adult swim cartoon. Apart from that the graphics are simplistic so don't expect anything crazy.

Audio:

The audio design is great and actually quite surprising. There's a bit of voice acting in the game for two characters one of them is The narrator who is voiced by the developer of the game and he does a great job voicing him and his style of delivery where his lines are broken English is great and gives the game charm straight away. Then there is Gwen who has left audio logs all over the building giving you some backstory of the place and what went on in the every day life the voice actor for him also does a great job performing the character perfectly. 

The music is also great, while there's not much of music throughout the game, all the tracks you hear in the game are great. While not a track in the game, I really enjoyed one part where you have to complete a Waltz and your actions play musical cues in the game world and I liked it a lot. 

Gameplay:

Bucket Detective is really simplistic, so don't expect a massive game. At it's heart it's a walking simulator, but again there is a lot more to do than in usual walking simulator s. The game is short, but there are some puzzles to complete and even though there's not many of them, all of them are unique and cool to figure out. 

The game is short, but it does have some cool features to  extend play time, like a directors commentary and multiple endings to see how the story wraps up all of them messed up in their own way. 

Verdict:

Bucket Detective is a weird game, but as stated before if you played The static speaks my name you know what to expect out of the game. This game is not for the easily offended cause it does joke about some dark stuff and there's some disturbing elements. But if you can look past that, you can expect quite a deep game, even though it might look shallow. 

Final Rating:
8/10

Pros:
+ Story is weird, but good 
+ Puzzles are unique and fun to solve
+ Sound design is great

Cons:
- Not many puzzles
- Might be too offensive for some people
